advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the `ts_seconds(stamp)` call in parse_logs so a malformed/tz-less timestamp is counted (e.g. audit['malformed_timestamp']) and the record skipped, per the documented 'counted and skipped' contract.
evidence: scripts/rebar_duration_probe_support.py:369-373: `try: record = json.loads(raw) except json.JSONDecodeError: audit["malformed_line"] += 1; continue`
scripts/rebar_duration_probe_support.py:376-378: `if not isinstance(stamp, str) or not isinstance(payload, dict): continue` then `when = ts_seconds(stamp)`

ts_seconds raises: `raise ValueError("timestamp must include a timezone offset")` and `datetime.fromisoformat` itself raises ValueError on unparseable strings; the isinstance(stamp,str) guard only ensures it is a string, not a valid ISO8601 timestamp
Docstring in scripts/rebar_duration_probe.py: 'Malformed records are counted and skipped.'
advisory.finding: `when = ts_seconds(stamp)` at line 378 is outside the try/except that guards record parsing; `ts_seconds` raises `ValueError` on a malformed or timezone-less `timestamp` string, so a single bad record raises an uncaught exception that aborts the entire log scan — directly contradicting the module docstring's promise that 'Malformed records are counted and skipped.'
scenarios: A rollout JSONL contains a record whose `timestamp` is a non-ISO string or lacks a tz offset — the whole run crashes instead of counting/skipping the record.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the parse: `try: when = ts_seconds(stamp) except ValueError: audit["malformed_timestamp"] += 1; continue`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an audit counter for the `data`-not-a-dict skip in _completion_phase_timestamps so malformed phase events are counted rather than silently dropped.
evidence: scripts/rebar_duration_probe_support.py:480-482: `data = raw.get("data")` / `if not isinstance(data, dict): continue` (no audit increment)
Contrast: line 478 `audit["bad_phase_event"] += 1` and line 492 `audit["bad_phase_timestamp"] += 1` DO count anomalies
advisory.finding: In `_completion_phase_timestamps`, records whose top-level `raw` is valid JSON but whose `data` is not a dict are silently skipped with no audit counter, unlike the `bad_phase_event`/`bad_phase_timestamp` counters used elsewhere in the same function — a malformed-but-parseable phase event becomes invisible rather than counted.
scenarios: A STATUS/SIGNATURE json file with a non-dict `data` field is dropped without any diagnostic, so an operator cannot tell whether phase timestamps were absent or silently discarded.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a parse_logs test whose initial exec output contains terminal markers but no wall_time_seconds, asserting invocation.end/duration is set and audit['terminal_text_fallback'] increments.
evidence: Added code: `if terminal:\n    wrapper.invocation.end = when\n    audit["terminal_text_fallback"] += 1`

Named violating input never tested: an `exec` initial call whose output is text like `... "verdict": "PASS" ...` with no `wall_time_seconds` JSON object — expected to set invocation.end via fallback and bump `terminal_text_fallback`.

Test functions present (search_files) cover parse_logs only via `test_parse_logs_links_initial_yield_and_pty_poll` (wall_time_seconds present) and `test_parse_logs_audits_unknown_yielded_cell`; neither exercises the terminal-text fallback.
Added code: `if meaningful and any(item not in WRAPPERS for item in meaningful):\n    continue`
Named violating input untested: `classify_command("foo && rebar review-plan sample-ticket")` should return `[]` (foo is not a wrapper), but no test asserts this rejection.

Existing classify tests (`test_classify_command_separates_gate_operations_and_exclusions`, `test_classify_command_unwraps_shell_command_strings`) only use wrapper prefixes (rtk/proxy) that are accepted.
advisory.finding: The `terminal_text_fallback` branch in `parse_logs`'s `finish` closure is newly added and untested: when a result object with `wall_time_seconds` is absent but the flushed text contains terminal markers (e.g. a `review-plan` output containing `"verdict"`/`PASS`/`BLOCK`, or a `close` output containing `transitioned `), it sets `invocation.end = when` and increments `audit['terminal_text_fallback']`. No test drives an initial exec whose output has terminal markers but no `wall_time_seconds`, so this duration-reconstruction fallback (which determines an invocation's `duration`) is never exercised.
merged_from: classify_command's prefix-rejection guard (`if meaningful and any(item not in WRAPPERS for item in meaningful): continue`) is newly added and untested. This branch discards a `rebar` invocation preceded by a non-wrapper command in a compound line, distinguishing real gate invocations from incidental mentions. No test supplies a command like `some-other-cmd && rebar review-plan t` to confirm the invocation is rejected, so a regression that mis-classifies such lines would not be caught.
